A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ODDR research and have readable text, equations, tables and figures. V2 includes Section 7 appendices; the supplied v1 ends with references. Results absent from v1's PDF are assessed as newly documented, without assuming the underlying experiments were newly performed.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification and object-detection experiments on ImageNet, Caltech-101, INRIA and CASIA, including defense comparisons and Grad-CAM examples.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds depth-estimation results, additional model and attack evaluations, ablations, sensitivity analyses and an adaptive-attack evaluation.

M1.justification: V1's Algorithm 1 selects the largest outlier cluster and neutralizes one mask. V2 selects all clusters meeting a new minPts threshold and applies SVD to a mask around each cluster. This substantively extends the procedure to multiple suspicious regions while retaining the fragmentation, Isolation Forest and SVD components.

E1.justification: V2 adds KITTI monocular depth estimation under SSAP attacks, dynamic and deformable classification attacks through GDPA and Shape Matters, multiple-patch detection examples, and a defense-aware adaptive-attack scenario. The original classification and detection datasets and naturalistic-patch evaluations remain.

E2.justification: V2 adds DR, identified as DefensiveDR, as an evaluated defense in Table 4 and supplies LGS/Jedi comparisons for LAVAN beyond v1's reported GoogleAP comparison. This is a limited expansion of the comparator set. Jujutsu, De-randomized Smoothing and PatchGuard disappear from the comparison table but their original comparison scores remain in Section 4.3.

E3.justification: V2 adds Inception-v3, ViT and Swin classification settings, a Faster-RCNN evaluation on an INRIA subset, and MIMdepth evaluation using depth error, affected-region ratio and MSE against clean predictions. It also introduces parameter-sweep and adaptive-attack protocols. Section 5.4 states 100 isolation trees while Section 4.2 retains v1's 500, so the actual revised tree budget is unresolved.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's naturalistic-patch and Grad-CAM analyses, v2 adds Isolation Forest versus DBSCAN localization comparisons, neutralization alternatives, comparison with dimension reduction alone, hyperparameter sensitivity curves, computational-cost measurements, and adaptive-attack distribution diagnostics. Sections 5.1–5.6 and 7.5–7.6 substantially expand investigation of component effectiveness and robustness.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2's Gaussian fits and Mahalanobis plots characterize image-fragment distributions; they do not introduce uncertainty reporting for the reported performance results.

E6.justification: Most matched original classification and detection scores are retained. V2 adds extensive results, including 83.1% ViT accuracy under GoogleAP, KITTI depth error decreasing from 0.59 to 0.11 with ODDR, and larger-patch results in Tables 7–10. These are additional settings, not demonstrated improvements over v1 under identical conditions. ResNet-152/GoogleAP adversarial accuracy is inconsistently reported as 39.3 in v2's main tables versus 39.9 in v1 and v2's appendix.

T1.justification: The Isolation Forest scoring equations and truncated-SVD mathematics are retained. V2 adds computational-complexity claims in Section 5.3 and formal Gaussian moment constraints for the adaptive attack, supported by Mahalanobis-distance analysis in Section 7.6. These are limited mathematical extensions; no new theorem or proof is provided.

C1.justification: V2 explicitly extends the main contribution to monocular depth estimation and demonstrated effectiveness on Transformer architectures. Its abstract replaces v1's broad claims of performance within 1–3% or 3–5% of clean baselines with a specific GoogleAP comparison. The introduction also adds a depth-error reduction claim.

C2.justification: V2 introduces a substantive adaptive-attack interpretation: matching clean-image distributions makes patches harder to isolate but allegedly weakens their attack effectiveness. It also attributes gains over DR to outlier detection and interprets parameter sensitivity and CPU timings as supporting practical deployment. V1 lacks these analyses of mechanism and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies a 1,000-image classification test sample, additional hyperparameter ranges and minPts values, CPU hardware and processing times, and adaptive-attack constraints. Appendices describe a sample-folder structure and disclose that the code is proprietary and cannot be openly shared. These are substantial documentation additions, although the conflicting tree counts limit reproducibility and the described folders are not included in the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands its research context through DefensiveDR, GDPA, Shape Matters, SSAP, monocular depth estimation, Transformer architectures and distribution-analysis literature. The explicit comparison with DefensiveDR also positions outlier detection as the source of additional benefit over dimension reduction alone. Moving the retained empirical-versus-certified defense discussion into the introduction is a separate presentation change.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, contributions and experimental discussion. Related work is integrated into the introduction, the standalone Key Findings subsection is removed, and the discussion is reorganized into six subsections. Isolation-tree material and retained clean-sample results move into a substantial appendix.

P2.justification: V2 consolidates classification results into a larger table and merges the separate INRIA/CASIA comparison tables. It relocates the overview diagram, redraws the detailed pipeline in the appendix, removes v1's patch gallery, and adds depth/detection examples, sensitivity plots and distribution plots. Appendix tables expand the original patch-size displays; Table 11 repeats Table 4 rather than providing another experiment.

improvement.justification: V1 offered little direct empirical scrutiny of component choices, parameter sensitivity or defense-aware attacks. V2's ablations, sensitivity curves and adaptive-attack diagnostics substantially improve assessment of the mechanism and its limits, while depth-estimation and Transformer experiments meaningfully test broader applicability. Conflicting 100/500-tree settings and 39.3/39.9 GoogleAP values weaken reproducibility, but the added scrutiny and supporting evidence provide a substantial net improvement.
